title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Over a field k of characteristic ≠ 2, take an elliptic curve E with Weierstrass-type model ℘'^2 = ℘^3 + a1℘^2 + a2℘ + a3. Here z = ℘ is the coordinate on P^1 = E/{±1}. The roots ξ1, ξ2, ξ3 of f(z) = z^3 + a1 z^2 + a2 z + a3 are the x-coordinates of the 2-torsion points ε_i. With the sign conventions used, ξ_jξ_k = −a3/ξ_i and Σ ξ_iξ_j = a2.

The involution σ_i. Translation x ↦ x + ε_i commutes with −1, so it descends to an involution σ_i of P^1. This involution swaps ξ_i with ∞ and ξ_j with ξ_k. The previous page determined it as the Möbius map σ_i z = (ξ_i z + b_i)/(z − ξ_i), with b_i = ξ_jξ_k − ξ_i(ξ_j + ξ_k).

Rewriting b_i. On this page Grothendieck uses symmetric functions: b_i = 2ξ_jξ_k − a2 = −(a2 + 2a3/ξ_i). This gives (62): σ_i z = (ξ_i z − (a2 + 2a3/ξ_i))/(z − ξ_i).

Fixed points. The fixed-point divisor Δ_i of σ_i is cut out by z^2 − 2ξ_i z + (a2 + 2a3/ξ_i) = 0, equation (63). Its roots are z = ξ_i ± √(ξ_i^2 − a2 − 2a3/ξ_i), equation (64). Using ξ_i^3 = −a1ξ_i^2 − a2ξ_i − a3, he rewrites the radicand as −(1/ξ_i)(a1ξ_i^2 + 2a2ξ_i + 3a3), equation (65).

Meaning of the fixed points. A fixed point of σ_i is the image of a point x with x + ε_i = ±x. The nontrivial case is 2x = ε_i, i.e. x is a 4-torsion point halving ε_i. So the two roots are the ℘-values of the four points x with 2x = ε_i. Over the three indices i this gives 6 of the x-coordinates of 4-torsion points.

Purpose. This feeds the next page. There, choosing x_i with 2x_i = ε_i amounts to choosing z_i (2 choices) and then z_i' with z_i'^2 = f(z_i) (2 choices), which matches the ambiguity in ₂E(k). The 'Jacobi pinning of relative level 4', Σ x_i = 0, then becomes a collinearity (3×3 determinant) condition on the points (z_i, z_i'). The whole computation serves an explicit description of level-4 rigidifications on the moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2.

Modern form. The radicand equals ξ_i^2 + b_i = (ξ_i − ξ_j)(ξ_i − ξ_k) = f'(ξ_i). Equivalently ξ_i·(radicand) = 3ξ_i^3 + 2a1ξ_i^2 + a2ξ_i. This is the classical halving formula x(P) = e_i ± √((e_i − e_j)(e_i − e_k)) for 2P = (e_i, 0).
errors: Not an error but a missed simplification. The radicand in (64)/(65) is exactly f'(ξ_i) = 3ξ_i^2 + 2a1ξ_i + a2 = (ξ_i − ξ_j)(ξ_i − ξ_k), a polynomial in ξ_i. Grothendieck's form −(1/ξ_i)(a1ξ_i^2 + 2a2ξ_i + 3a3) divides by ξ_i. This needlessly raises the marginal worry about the case ξ_i = 0, which the form f'(ξ_i) avoids entirely.

Marginal formula for ξ_i = 0, as transcribed: −(a1ξ_i + 2a2 + 3ξ_jξ_k). The correct substitution a3/ξ_i = −ξ_jξ_k gives −(a1ξ_i + 2a2) + 3ξ_jξ_k. For ξ_i = 0 this yields a2 = ξ_jξ_k, as it should; the transcribed sign would give −5a2. Either the transcription or Grothendieck has a sign slip; the image is hard to read here.

The text says 'compte tenu de (66)', but the relation used, ξ_i^3 = −a1ξ_i^2 − a2ξ_i − a3, is equation (10) of the previous page. Equation (66) appears only on the next page. Either this is a misreading or a forward/garbled reference.

ideas.what: Translation by a 2-torsion point descends to a Möbius involution of E/±1 = P^1 exchanging e_i↔∞ and e_j↔e_k, with explicit formula
ideas.modern_name: Translation by 2-torsion acting on the Kummer line / x-line (Möbius involution)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weierstrass/Jacobi era; standard in elliptic function theory)

ideas.what: Fixed points of σ_i are the x-coordinates of the points P with 2P = ε_i, given by x = ξ_i ± √((ξ_i−ξ_j)(ξ_i−ξ_k))
ideas.modern_name: Halving formula for 2-torsion / x-coordinates of 4-torsion points (cf. 2-descent)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (19th century; standard in Cassels, Knapp, Silverman–Tate)

ideas.what: Use of these explicit half-points to express a level-4 'Jacobi pinning' Σx_i = 0 (continued on next page)
ideas.modern_name: Level-4 structures / theta-type rigidification of elliptic curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (theta relations); Igusa and Mumford for level structures in modern form

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine, correct computation of the classical halving formula for 2-torsion on a Weierstrass cubic. It is done slightly circuitously: Grothendieck misses that the radicand is simply f'(ξ_i). Nothing new or uncredited appears.
transcription_corrections: 'parmi les dix points z_i' should almost certainly read 'six points z_i'. There are 3 indices × 2 roots = 6 x-coordinates of points halving the ε_i.
The insertion '{+d'ordre 2 de E+}' is more plausibly 'd'ordre 4 de E', since the roots are ℘-values of points x with 2x = ε_i, which have order 4.
'compte tenu de (66)' is probably a reference to (10) (the cubic relation), or a misreading of it.
The margin formula sign for the ξ_i = 0 case is uncertain; mathematically it should be −(a1ξ_i + 2a2) + 3ξ_jξ_k.
